title: Reading music notes
examples: How many lines are on the stave?
What does the treble clef tell us?
If a note is longer, does it sound louder?

explain.say: Today we are learning how to read music notes. We will look at the lines and spaces first. This helps us know where the notes sit.
The treble clef tells us the pitch of the music. It curls around a line to show us where a certain note is. This is very important to know.
The notes have names that follow a pattern. On the lines, the names are E, G, B, D, and F. These are easy to remember.

draw.text: Line Notes: E G B D F

explain.say: The spaces also have names, and they follow a pattern too. The spaces spell out the word F A C E. This helps us read them quickly.

draw.text: Space Notes: F A C E

explain.say: Notes have different lengths, which tells us how long to sing them. A whole note is the longest one we see.
In real life, music uses these notes all the time. Think about a simple song you know well. You can count the beats to know the note lengths.

faq.q: Why does the treble clef look like a fancy swirl?
faq.a: The treble clef is a symbol that tells us the pitch. It helps musicians know which notes sound high or low.
asks: How do I read the clef?

faq.q: Are the notes on the lines always the same names?
faq.a: Yes, the lines always follow the pattern E, G, B, D, F from bottom to top. This is a fixed rule in music.

faq.q: If a note is big, does that mean it is louder?
faq.a: No, the size of the note head does not mean loudness. The note length tells us how long to hold the sound.
asks: Is note size related to volume?

faq.q: Do the spaces spell a word?
faq.a: Yes, the spaces spell out the word F A C E. This is a helpful trick for remembering the names of the spaces.
asks: What word do the spaces spell?
How do I remember the space notes?

faq.q: Can I read music without knowing the clef?
faq.a: It is very difficult to read accurately without knowing the clef. The clef sets the pitch standard for the entire piece.
asks: What happens if I ignore the clef?

facts: The stave has five lines and four spaces.
The treble clef indicates the pitch for the notes.
The line notes, from bottom to top, are E, G, B, D, F.
The space notes spell the word F A C E.

quiz.say: If a note is written on the second line from the bottom, what is its name?
quiz.why: The second line from the bottom is G, following the pattern E, G, B, D, F.

wrong.0: B is the name on the third line, which is higher up.
wrong.1: D is the name on the fourth line, which is higher still.
wrong.3: This is the name of the bottom line, not the second line.

quiz.say: Which note name correctly belongs in the space directly above the bottom line?
quiz.why: The spaces spell F A C E, so the first space after the bottom line is F.

wrong.1: A is the second space, not the first one.
wrong.2: E is a line note, not a space note.
wrong.3: C is the third space, which is higher up.
